term: labeled real-line spatial configuration and translation profile
definition: Bodies are labels B and a configuration is B→ℝ in a chosen absolute coordinate. A common shift adds a real displacement to every label. Selected relative data are signed pairwise displacements, stronger than unsigned distances. Origin normalization subtracts one labeled body’s coordinate; it represents a translation orbit and asserts no actual absolute location. This static profile contains no dynamics, rotation, empirical completeness or metaphysical-identity criterion.
note: Analyst geometry, reusing Mathlib real normed-group arithmetic and metric. The Certificate explicitly supplies a body where inhabitedness matters and also includes an empty-domain control. A real line is a bounded mathematical model, not a replacement for three-dimensional mechanics.
